speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe how your double vision changes when you look to the sides versus when you look straight ahead? Additionally, when you attempt to climb stairs or lift your arms, do you feel a distinct weakness or a sensation that you are losing control?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Did you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing or speaking recently? REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibodies, Repetitive Nerve Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-AChR antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive Nerve Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Anti-AChR antibodies combined with the clinical presentation of fluctuating muscle weakness and diplopia confirms this diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck and Chest CT to evaluate for thymoma.
